title: var in a loop
explanation: var is function-scoped, so all three callbacks share one i, and it equals 3 by the time they run. let creates a new binding on each iteration.

title: Default sort
explanation: The default sort converts values to strings and compares them as text, so "10" sorts before "9". Use .sort((a, b) => a - b).

title: typeof
explanation: This is a historical bug from the first version of JS that was never fixed. Check for null with x === null.

title: Equality
explanation: "" is coerced to 0, and null only loosely equals undefined. NaN never equals anything, itself included, so use Number.isNaN.

title: Event loop
prompt: In what order are the numbers logged?
explanation: Synchronous code runs first (1, 4). Then the microtask queue runs (promise callbacks, 3), and after that macrotasks such as setTimeout (2).

title: Spot the bug
prompt: What does total(ids) resolve to? (price() is async and returns a positive number.)
explanation: forEach ignores the promises the callback returns, so total returns before any await finishes. Use for...of with await, or Promise.all.

title: Object key order
explanation: Integer-like keys come first in ascending order. All other string keys follow in insertion order.

title: map + parseInt
explanation: map passes (value, index), so this calls parseInt("2", 1) and parseInt("3", 2). Radix 1 is invalid, and 3 isn't a binary digit, so both give NaN.

title: Object.freeze
explanation: freeze is shallow: o.inner can't be reassigned, but the nested object can still be changed. You have to freeze each nested object as well.
